metaDescription: Six 1500W electric space heaters compared on heating type, noise, oscillation, remotes and safety, with plain advice on circuits, coverage and cord safety.
expertTake: The DREO 319 is the pick for most bedrooms and offices: a ceramic PTC element, a brushless DC fan, 70 degree oscillation, a remote and a full set of listed safety features. The Amazon Basics ceramic is the value pick for a desk or a small room. Anyone who wants whole-room heat from a heater alone should skip all of these: every 1500W plug-in heater produces the same heat, so the choice is about noise, controls and safety.
introParagraphs: Every 1500 watt plug-in heater turns electricity into heat at essentially full efficiency, so the amount of heat is the same whatever the shape or price. What changes between models is how the heat is delivered, how loud the fan is, how well it protects against tipping and overheating, and how easy it is to control. Check the circuit and the cord before you check the brand.

This guide explains what to check on the circuit before you plug one in, how ceramic, infrared and tower designs differ, and which safety features matter. Use the picks above as a shortlist, then read the reviews to choose by the room you want to warm and the noise you can live with.

products.name: DREO 319 1500W Quiet Space Heater with Remote and 70 Degree Oscillation

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Child lock, tip-over, V0 flame retardant

products.description:
The DREO 319 earns the top spot because it pairs a ceramic PTC element, which limits its own temperature, with a brushless DC fan. A brushless motor is quieter and more efficient than a brushed fan, which matters in a bedroom where the heater runs all night. The listing also names a 70 degree oscillation, an 11.5 feet per second airflow figure, a remote, a child lock, tip-over protection and V0 flame retardant plastic.

PTC stands for positive temperature coefficient: as the ceramic warms, its resistance rises and the current falls, so the element throttles itself and cannot glow red. That self-limiting behavior is one of the safest ways to make heat from a small element. Compared with the Amazon Basics, the DREO adds oscillation, a quiet fan and a remote for the same wattage.

In use, place it on a hard, level floor with three feet of clear space, and plug it straight into a wall outlet. Do not use an extension cord or power strip. Vacuum the intake grille monthly, since dust is the usual source of a burning smell at the start of the season. Run it for a night with a bedside thermometer to learn how long it takes to reach your target, then use the timer to start it an hour before bed instead of leaving it on. A smart plug is not a good idea for a heater unless the plug is rated for the full 12.5 amps.
products.bestFor: A bedroom or office where low noise, oscillation and a remote matter.
pros: Brushless DC fan for quiet running
Remote, child lock and tip-over protection
cons: Costs more than basic ceramic heaters

products.name: Amazon Basics Ceramic Space Heater 1500W Compact with Thermostat
products.description:
Amazon Basics sells the plain version: a ceramic heater with three settings (1500W high, 900W low and a fan-only mode), a thermostat and standard safety features. It weighs 3 lb and measures 7.5 by 6.3 by 9.5 inches, small enough for a desk or the floor under it. The listing names overheat and tip-over protection and a power indicator light.

The low setting at 900W is useful because it uses much less power and keeps a small room comfortable once it is warm. Compared with the DREO 319, it has no remote, no oscillation and a simpler fan, so it is louder per unit of air but costs less. For a desk or a bathroom doorway, simple is fine.

Because it is small, the heat plume is narrow, so aim it at where you sit. Keep it away from curtains and paper, and do not leave it running unattended in a room with pets. For a desk, place it to the side so the airflow crosses your legs instead of pointing at your face, and keep paper and cables clear of the front grille. Switch it to the low setting once the area is warm, which roughly halves the power.
products.bestFor: A desk, a bathroom doorway or a small bedroom where a simple heater is enough.

products.name: Dr Infrared Heater DR-968 1500W Portable Space Heater
products.description:
The DR-968 combines an infrared quartz tube with a PTC element, so you get radiant heat that warms people and objects directly plus fan-blown warm air. The listing states 12.5 amps, which is exactly what 1500W draws at 120V, plus a 39 dB noise level, a 12 hour automatic shutoff and an infrared remote.

Infrared heating feels warm quickly on your skin because it heats objects in line of sight, not just the air. That makes it well suited to a seat in a cool room. The 12.5 amp figure is also a useful reminder that the heater takes most of a 15 amp circuit's safe capacity, leaving little for anything else on the same breaker.

Compared with the DREO, the DR-968 trades oscillation for a hybrid heat source. It is a bigger, older design, so check the dimensions. Dust the quartz tube gently with the unit off and cool. Radiant heaters feel strongest in a straight line, so move the seat or the heater until the warm patch lands where you sit. Let the quartz tube cool before moving the unit, and never cover it with a blanket.
products.bestFor: A living-room seat or workspace where radiant heat on your body feels best.
cons: Takes most of a 15 amp circuit

products.name: Lasko 751320 23 Inch Ceramic Tower Space Heater with Remote

specList.label: Safety
specList.value: Self-regulating element, overheat protection, cool-touch housing

products.description:
Lasko's 23 inch tower stands upright with a narrow footprint, wide oscillation and a remote that controls heat settings, oscillation and a timer. The listing mentions a self-regulating ceramic element, overheat protection and cool-touch housing, and an ETL certification mark, which indicates the unit was evaluated to a recognized safety standard.

A tower is a good fit for a living room corner because it takes little floor space and sends warm air out wide. The tradeoff is stability: a taller body tips more easily on a soft rug, though tip-over protection cuts power if it falls. Compared with the DREO, the Lasko is a taller, more traditional heater with a long track record.

Lasko has made heaters and fans for decades, and spare parts and manuals are easy to find. Keep it on a hard floor, away from foot traffic, and vacuum the rear intake. Move it with two hands from the base, not the top, since the narrow tower can shift its weight. Clean the rear intake with a vacuum brush at the start of each season so the first hours of use do not smell of burnt dust.
products.bestFor: A living room or bedroom corner where a slim, wide-sweeping heater suits the layout.
cons: Tall body is easier to knock over

products.name: BLACK+DECKER BHDC201 Personal Ceramic Heater 1500W
products.description:
The BHDC201 is the small personal heater from a well-known tool brand: fan only, 750W low and 1500W high, with a power-on indicator light and overheat protection. It is meant for an office desk or a small personal space. The listing frames it as a desk heater rather than a room heater.

A personal heater warms what is near it, so place it close and aim it at your legs. The 750W low setting is half the power and a common choice for a quiet desk. Against the Amazon Basics, it offers the same idea with a different brand name and a lower middle setting.

As with any heater, plug it into the wall, not into a power strip, and unplug it when you leave. Dust the vents monthly. If the small body shuts off on its overheat protection, it is usually because the intake is blocked by a curtain or a stack of papers. Unplug it, clear the obstruction, wait a few minutes and restart it.
products.bestFor: An office desk or a bedside table where a small, familiar heater is enough.
cons: Short on features compared with the DREO

products.name: AUBKN X-Large 1500W Space Heater 24 Inch Oscillating with Remote
products.description:
AUBKN builds a 24 inch tower around a 1500W PTC ceramic element with 70 degree oscillation, a thermostat, ECO modes and a 1 to 12 hour programmable timer, plus a remote. The tall format and wide oscillation make it a living-room heater more than a desk heater.

ECO mode cycles the element to hold a target temperature with less energy, which is useful because it means the heater is not at full draw all the time. The programmable timer lets you set it to switch off after you fall asleep. Compared with the Lasko tower, the AUBKN adds the thermostat and ECO details.

A lesser-known brand means support is less certain. Check the safety certification on the unit and the plug, and register the warranty. Because it is tall, anchor the cord loosely so a passing foot does not pull the unit over, and put it on the hard floor rather than a rug. Use the timer and ECO modes together to avoid a night of constant full-power running.
products.bestFor: A larger living room or bedroom where a tall, oscillating tower with ECO mode fits.
pros: 70 degree oscillation on a tall tower
cons: Tall body needs a stable floor

buyingCriteria.explanation: A US 120V 15 amp circuit can safely support about 1800W continuous, which is why portable heaters stop at 1500W. 1500W produces about 5,120 BTU an hour whatever the type. The Dr Infrared's 12.5 amp rating shows how much of the circuit one heater uses. Count what else is on the circuit, because a vacuum or hair dryer starting alongside a heater can trip the breaker.

Ceramic PTC models like the DREO 319 and AUBKN warm air quickly and limit their own element temperature. The Dr Infrared adds radiant heat that warms objects directly. Oil-filled radiators, not in this list, are slow and silent. Pick by how you sit and how quickly you want warmth. A mixed approach is to use infrared at your desk and a ceramic fan heater for the room.

A common rule is 10 watts per square foot, so 1500W suits roughly 150 square feet of insulated room. A larger or drafty room will not reach target temperature. No tower or oscillation changes that total output. Measure your room, multiply the square feet by ten, and compare the result with 1500.

DREO lists 34 dB on some models and the Dr Infrared lists 39 dB, both low figures. A brushless DC fan, like the DREO 319 uses, is quieter than a brushed fan. Fans on cheap ceramics are often 45 to 55 dB. Listen to a unit in a quiet room before you decide, since fan pitch is as annoying as volume.

Look for tip-over shutoff, overheat protection, a cool-touch housing and a recognized listing mark such as ETL, which the Lasko cites. A heater whose plug warms noticeably is a red flag. Never plug a heater into a power strip or an extension cord. Check that the plug shows a safety mark and a thick cord, and avoid thin cords.

A thermostat holds temperature and saves energy. A timer such as the AUBKN's 1 to 12 hours shuts it off after you fall asleep. A remote is convenient for a tower. Simple dials like the Amazon Basics are more robust. For a heater that will run unattended, a thermostat is not optional.

specDecoder.meaning: Electrical power input. For resistance heaters it equals heat output. It sets total heat, not feel.
Current draw, watts divided by volts. 1500W at 120V is 12.5 amps. It also tells you how much of a circuit the unit uses.
Positive temperature coefficient ceramic. It self-limits its own temperature. It stops the element from overheating on its own.
A safety listing mark showing the unit was evaluated to a recognized standard. It does not replace checking the plug and cord.
Sweeping the airflow side to side. It spreads the heat but adds no output. It improves coverage but not total heat.
specDecoder.watchFor: The DREO and AUBKN list 70 degrees.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tip-over, overheat and listing marks. The Lasko's ETL mark and the DREO's V0 plastic stood out. A recognized safety listing counted for more than a marketing claim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated decibel figures and fan types. The DREO and Dr Infrared publish figures, based on the spec sheet. Stated decibel figures counted for more than the word quiet.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat delivery
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated ceramic, infrared and tower designs. The Dr Infrared adds radiant heat. A hybrid element counted as a real difference.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted thermostats, timers and remotes. The AUBKN's 1 to 12 hour timer is the most flexible. Programmable timers counted as safety features.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed brand history and price tier, judged against owner feedback patterns. We evaluated every pick against the same checklist. Established brands received a modest trust credit.

maintenance.why: Dust reduces airflow and causes burning smells. Unplug and let it cool first. A soft brush attachment is best.
A warm plug or frayed cord is a fire risk. Stop using the heater if you see damage. A warm plug is a reason to stop using it.
Dust left inside burns off next winter. A quick vacuum prevents it. Store it in its box in a dry place.
Tilt it carefully while on a hard floor and confirm that it shuts off. Test it on a hard floor.
A loose or scorched outlet is unsafe for a 12.5 amp load. Replace it if worn. A scorched outlet needs an electrician.

faq.q: Can I plug a space heater into a power strip?
faq.a: No. Plug it directly into a wall outlet. Power strips and extension cords can overheat at 12.5 amps. Use a dedicated circuit if possible. If a breaker trips, move the heater to a different circuit and unplug other appliances.

faq.q: Is a more expensive heater hotter?
faq.a: No. All 1500W resistance heaters deliver the same heat. Price buys quieter fans, remotes, better safety and nicer build. A cheap hygrometer will also show you how dry the air gets when the heater runs for hours.

faq.q: How big a room will it heat?
faq.a: About 150 square feet of insulated space, using 10 watts per square foot. Larger or drafty rooms need a bigger heat source. If your room is cold because of drafts, sealing the gaps does more than a bigger heater.
Ceramic warms air and suits rooms. Infrared warms objects and suits a seat. The Dr Infrared combines both. Do not place a heater under a window with curtains, where fabric can blow into the grille.

faq.q: Is it safe to leave one on overnight?
faq.a: Only with tip-over and overheat protection, clear space and a thermostat or timer. Many fire services advise against sleeping with a heater running. A heater with a tip-over switch and a timer is the safest overnight choice, but it still needs clear space.

faq.q: How much does it cost to run?
faq.a: At 1500W, one hour uses 1.5 kWh. Multiply by your rate to get the cost. A thermostat reduces the hours of full draw. Your utility bill will show the effect in a month, so keep a note of hours of use.
